K1.stone_why: The bold display and set numbers are faceted like chiselled inscription letters, while the regular titles stay a calm serif with only a faint hewn edge.
K1.carving_why: The facets on S, 3, 5, 6 and 8 share one polygonal logic and look deliberate, with the 6 bowl cleaner than K3's; 3/8 and 0/O are still easy to tell apart, though a few joins are slightly uneven.
K1.calm_why: Light regular titles and a measured bold give it presence without shouting, and the body text stays quiet.
K1.personality_why: The cut-stone bold numerals are recognisable, though the regular weight reads close to a conventional book serif.

K2.stone_why: It is a smooth, conventional transitional serif with curved bowls and no hewn quality, so only its classical proportions hint at an inscription.
K2.carving_why: There is no visible carving: S, 3, 5, 6 and 8 are fully smooth curves.
K2.calm_why: Calm and steady, but its display presence is a little ordinary next to the others.
K2.personality_why: A competent but generic book serif you would not pick out again.

K3.stone_why: Nearly identical to K1, with faceted bold capitals and digits that read as cut stone.
K3.carving_why: It uses the same polygonal system as K1, but the 6 and 5 bowls show slightly more irregular, lumpy facets, so the cuts look a bit less even and more processed.
K3.calm_why: It has the same quiet regular weight and measured bold, so it is calm with presence.
K3.personality_why: Its faceted numerals have the same distinct voice as K1.

K4.stone_why: Heavy, faceted letterforms throughout, including the regular titles, read most strongly as hewn blocks and inscription.
K4.carving_why: Facets are coherent and crisp across S, 3, 5, 6, 8 and the capitals, and the digits stay distinct, though at this weight a few corners look blunt and clotted.
K4.calm_why: The weight is heavy everywhere, including the titles and even the body text, which makes it dense and near-shouting rather than calm.
K4.personality_why: It has the most unmistakable and consistent carved-stone voice of the four.
